title: Burst catchup debt leak causing reserved-pool starvation — graded fallback plan and hotfix
creator: Maya Thompson
description: Summary: Several enterprise customers experienced 5–20% elevated 500/429 errors during a weekend traffic spike in ap-southeast-1. Root cause is a latent 'catchup debt' leak in the burst-credit reconciliation pipeline combined with a headroom calc that ignored pending reconciliation writes. The leak allowed tenant-level burst balance to be temporarily overstated, then suddenly corrected, draining reserved-pool headroom and causing the autoscaler to fail open in a way that prevented fallback routing from engaging quickly. This ticket tracks the emergency hotfix, short-term mitigations, and longer-term fixes and telemetry improvements.
repro_steps: Simulate multi-tenant burst: drive a sustained 3x qps spike for 15 minutes from 25 distinct tenant tokens
Introduce a transient DB lock on the burst ledgers service (simulate long GC/event loop pause) during reconciliation window
Observe that catchup reconciliation job queues up pending delta writes but does not commit; cumulative 'pending_catchup' metric rises
After lock release, reconcile writes apply bursts in one batch, causing headroom to suddenly drop and reserved-pool allocation to reassign (observe allocation failures and 429s)
Verify that fallback routing is delayed due to the scheduler ignoring 'pending_catchup' in headroom projection
timeline: 2026-02-20 03:10 UTC — First customer SRE reports increased 429s and cold-starts in ap-southeast-1
2026-02-20 03:22 UTC — On-call confirmed spike correlated with reserved-pool allocation failures; mitigation: temporary uplift of burst throttles for affected tenants
2026-02-20 04:05 UTC — Investigating team identified high 'pending_catchup' backlog in ledger service and a correlation with recent kernel upgrade deploy
2026-02-20 06:40 UTC — Emergency patch deployed to autoscaler: cap immediate burst consumption and prioritize fallback routing; 429 rate dropped to baseline
2026-02-21 — Post-incident analysis began; deeper root cause identified as non-idempotent catchup write path and headroom projection bug
investigation_notes: The catchup service uses batched delta writes to the tenant burst ledger. Under transient DB contention the batch is retried but not fully idempotent, leading to an inconsistent 'pending' vs 'committed' state.

Headroom projection pipeline reads only 'committed_balance' and omits 'pending_catchup' entries. When pending writes apply atomically after lock release, headroom drops without a gradual backoff — causing rapid reserved pool depletion.
Fallback routing has a timing window that waits for autoscaler confirmation; in these races the confirmation was delayed because the autoscaler was overloaded with reconciliation work.
Telemetry gaps: no alert tracked 'pending_catchup' queue depth or reconciliation latency per-tenant; runbooks assumed reconciliation was near-instant.
There is a risk of double-counting if catchup retries are applied without idempotency keys; we saw 1.8x effective consumption on one tenant in logs before correction.
root_cause: Combination of (a) non-idempotent batched catchup writes that sometimes commit in a single large delta after DB contention, (b) headroom projection that ignores pending reconciliation writes, and (c) autoscaler/fallback timing assumptions that expect near-zero reconciliation latency. Together these caused abrupt reserved-pool headroom drops and delayed fallback activation.
mitigation: Short-term: deploy autoscaler throttle caps per-tenant, increase reserved-pool soft-headroom buffer by 12% for the region, and enable expedited fallback routing bypassing autoscaler confirmation. Medium-term: make catchup writes idempotent with a write-token, surface 'pending_catchup' in headroom projection, and add reconciliation latency SLOs and alerts. Long-term: redesign ledger reconciliation to support incremental commits and apply backpressure to tenant burst consumption when reconciliation lag > 2s.

rollback_plan: Hotfixes are small: if idempotency patch causes unexpected behavior, rollback to previous autoscaler binary and revert expedited fallback flag. Reserved-pool buffer is a config change and can be reverted via feature flag. Rollback steps documented in the release PR.
testing_plan: Unit tests for idempotent write tokens; integration test injecting DB lock and verifying no sudden headroom drop; staging canary in eu-west-1 with synthetic tenant load for 48h; load test to validate reserved-pool buffer prevents >5% 429s under 3x qps spike.
communication_plan: Customer-facing note drafted for affected tenants listing timeline, mitigations, and expected timeline for permanent fix. Internal postmortem to be shared with CSMs and AE team. On-call template and KC article updated.

postmortem_notes: Avoid single-batch commit patterns for tenant accounting systems where transient contention is possible.
Assume reconciliation latency > 0 for all projection algorithms and include 'pending' as a first-class input.
Improve runbook to include immediate reserved-pool buffer and expedited fallback as first mitigation steps for headroom depletion incidents.
Add regular chaos exercises that simulate ledger and DB contention during peak traffic windows.
